sections.label: The Models
paragraphs: Kimi K3 on max effort against GPT-6 Astra on low effort. Game 5 of ten, drafted fresh.
Nobody took a point of damage until turn 7. Both models spent the opening on mana, and the game was decided by which ramp deck converted first.

sections.label: Draft
paragraphs: Picks and reasoning are [[view:draft|here]], the final lists [[view:decks|here]].

Kimi drafted Gruul lands: [[card:Leaves from the Vine]] and [[card:Cycle of Renewal]] to ramp, [[card:Earthbending Lesson]] and [[card:Badgermole]] to animate those lands into attackers, and [[card:Bitter Work]] for cards.

Astra drafted Golgari sacrifice with the same lands theme pointed at a different payoff: [[card:Earthbender Ascension]] and [[card:Cycle of Renewal]] to ramp, [[card:Tolls of War]] making Ally tokens, and [[card:Hei Bai, Spirit of Balance]] plus [[card:The Fire Nation Drill]] as the finishers.

rounds.label: Turn 1
paragraphs: [[player:PilotA|Kimi K3]] takes the play with a smooth green hand and casts [[card:Leaves from the Vine]] on turn one.
[[player:PilotB|Astra]] leads on a tapped [[card:Kyoshi Village]] to set up [[card:Tolls of War]] next turn.

rounds.label: Turn 2
paragraphs: [[player:PilotA|Kimi K3]] plays a second Forest.
[[player:PilotB|Astra]] casts [[card:Tolls of War]], its Clue and token engine.

rounds.label: Turn 3
paragraphs: [[player:PilotA|Kimi K3]]'s Saga hits its second chapter with no creatures on board, so the trigger does nothing. It ramps with [[card:Cycle of Renewal]], sacrificing a tapped Forest to fetch two basics.
[[player:PilotB|Astra]] casts [[card:Earthbender Ascension]], animates the Village, and fetches a Swamp.

rounds.label: Turn 4
paragraphs: [[player:PilotA|Kimi K3]]'s third Saga chapter also finds nothing — no creature or Lesson in the graveyard to return. It animates a Mountain into a 4/4 with haste via [[card:Earthbending Lesson]] and attacks into a board whose only creature is tapped.

[[player:PilotB|Astra]] casts its own [[card:Cycle of Renewal]], sacrificing the animated Village so it returns — which triggers landfall, [[card:Tolls of War]] and the Ascension all at once, and fetches two lands.

rounds.label: Turn 5
paragraphs: [[player:PilotA|Kimi K3]] casts [[card:Bitter Work]] and keeps hitting with the animated Mountain.
[[player:PilotB|Astra]] is still assembling and takes the damage; it is on 12, Kimi untouched on 20.

rounds.label: Turn 6
paragraphs: [[player:PilotA|Kimi K3]] casts [[card:Earth Kingdom Soldier]], pumping the animated Mountain to 5/5, and attacks again.

[[player:PilotB|Astra]] finally turns the corner, and does it in one turn. [[card:The Fire Nation Drill]] arrives and immediately kills the Soldier, then Astra attacks with [[card:Hei Bai, Spirit of Balance]] and two Allies, sacrificing a Clue mid-combat to grow Hei Bai to 7/7. Twelve damage: Kimi goes from 16 to 4.

rounds.label: Turn 7
paragraphs: [[player:PilotA|Kimi K3]] attacks with the 5/5 Mountain, kills the blocking [[card:Fire Navy Trebuchet]], and adds [[card:Badgermole]] to animate another land. At 4 life it needs blockers more than attackers, and it has two.

[[player:PilotB|Astra]] has three. A land drop grows [[card:Hei Bai, Spirit of Balance]] to 8/8 with trample, the Drill is crewed with two 1/1 Allies that could not have attacked anyway, and the attack goes in with more trample damage than Kimi has blockers or life. Kimi dies on turn 14.

Both decks were built to turn lands into damage, and for six turns Kimi's version was strictly ahead — it had a 5/5 attacking while Astra had nothing. What Astra had instead was a board where every piece fed another: the Clue that grew Hei Bai, the land drop that gave it trample, the tokens that crewed the Drill for free. Kimi's 5/5 was one creature, and Astra's turn 6 killed everything else Kimi had.
